pages.title: Right Now
pages.content:
If I sent you this link instead of explaining something out loud, this is why. It is easier to write it once, carefully, than to say it well in the middle of things.

Current status · 17 August 2026

Blood pressure has been running high and has not settled overnight. Sleep is short. I saw my treating specialist on Sunday and we agreed I need a proper mental health plan, which does not exist yet. An echocardiogram is booked for Thursday 20 August. I am living in a caravan and have been without secure housing since early 2025.

This block is the only part of the site that changes. Everything else is background that stays true.

The rest of this page is permanent: what the pattern looks like, what actually helps, what is missing, and who to call. It does not go stale, so it is safe to keep the link.

If this is your first time reading it, start with The Pattern. If something is urgent right now, go straight to Who to Call.

pages.title: The Pattern, Plainly
pages.content:
Bipolar Affective Disorder is one of the diagnoses on my record. What follows is what it looks like from the inside, written down while I can still think clearly. It is a description, not a self-diagnosis. The formal picture is on What's On Record.

I go through stretches where output climbs steeply. Several projects at once across completely unrelated areas, all of them getting finished rather than just started. Sleep need drops, and the tiredness does not register the way it normally would. Ideas arrive fast and feel unusually clear.

The part people miss: it does not look like a crisis from outside. It looks like I am doing well. Calm, articulate, productive, on top of things. That smoothness is the signal, not the absence of one. If I seem more capable than usual and something still feels off to you, trust the second thing.

My body registers it before I do. Blood pressure that stays high and does not drop overnight has been the clearest physical marker so far. I have a documented cardiac history, so that is not a background detail.

There is a second thing worth knowing, because it has happened twice recently. Some weeks feel dreamlike and blurred, and I have found work I started with no memory of starting it. If I seem to have lost the thread of a conversation we definitely had, that is what is happening. Please just tell me plainly rather than assume I am being evasive.

High output is not evidence that I am well. It is frequently the first sign that I am not.

pages.title: What's On Record
pages.content:
None of this is self-assessed. It comes from a psychiatric report by Dr Winton-Brown dated 26 March 2025, and from earlier records accumulated across multiple admissions. I am putting it here so nobody has to take my word for any of it.

Diagnoses

Complex PTSD. The primary diagnosis, and the one Dr Winton-Brown assessed as fitting best. I agree with it.

Also carried: Borderline Personality Disorder. Bipolar Affective Disorder. Alcohol Use Disorder. Cannabis Use Disorder. These accumulated across multiple admissions from my late teens onward.

Where it started

Serious recurring illness from my late teens into my mid twenties, with multiple inpatient admissions. That period overlapped the deaths of my first musical mentor and my grandmother.

What a crisis has actually looked like

In April 2025 I presented to hospital twice within eleven days. Both were assessed as situational crisis. I was then admitted to PARC in Warrnambool for about four weeks from late April.

PARC worked. That matters more than anything else on this page, because it means there is a documented intervention that has already been effective once.

Every crisis so far has been situational, triggered by an identifiable event rather than arriving out of nowhere. That is a description of what has happened, not a promise about what will.

What was recommended, and never delivered

Integrated, consistent psychiatric care alongside trauma-directed psychological treatment, with substance-use support. It has never been consistently delivered, largely because I have not held a fixed address long enough to keep a place in a service. See What's Missing.

Substances, since it is always the next question

Alcohol: about six years abstinent, after roughly twenty years of heavy binge drinking that began at school.

Cannabis: heavy from around fifteen or sixteen. Reduced but ongoing, largely for anxiety.

The full report is held by me and by my solicitor, and has already been lodged with my housing application. If you need to see it rather than read a summary of it, ask me.

pages.title: If You're Trying to Help
pages.content:
Short version: say it plainly, say it once, and do not mistake calm for fine.

Things that actually help

  • Ask direct questions. "Have you slept? Have you eaten? When did you last sit down?" gets further than "are you okay?", which I will answer wrong out of habit.
  • Push for rest, not reassurance. I do not need to hear that the ideas are good. I need to hear that it is time to stop for the night.
  • Offer a lift. I do not have a driver's licence and I live in Koroit. Every appointment, pharmacy visit and meeting is in Warrnambool. Transport is a genuine barrier to my own care, not a small inconvenience.
  • Take the physical stuff seriously. Blood pressure especially. It is usually the more reliable signal, and it is the one I am most likely to wave off.
  • Say the serious thing once, clearly. I will hear it. I do not need it repeated four different ways, and repeating it makes me stop listening.

Things that do not

  • Do not argue me out of something mid-flow. It does not work and it burns the conversation. Suggest sleep, food or a pause instead of debating the idea itself.
  • Do not read high output as evidence things are fine. For me it is frequently the opposite signal.
  • Do not sit on a real concern to keep things comfortable. Awkward and said once beats smooth and unsaid.
  • Do not tell me to just see someone. I have been trying. See What's Missing for why that is harder than it sounds.

If something is genuinely urgent, skip to Who to Call.

pages.title: What's Actually Missing
pages.content:
This page exists because the most common response I get is a version of "have you thought about seeing someone." Yes. Repeatedly, for years. Here is where that actually stands.

No current mental health plan

I do not have a mental health care plan and I do not have a treating counsellor. My previous mental health social worker has fully retired and is no longer registered. He advised in August 2026 that he is not aware of local counsellors who bulk bill under a Medicare referral, and that most charge a gap fee. He was unusual in accepting the Medicare rebate alone for people on Centrelink payments.

The standing recommendation

Integrated, consistent psychiatric care alongside trauma-directed psychological treatment. That has been the documented recommendation since March 2025. It has never been able to be sustained.

The gap is financial and structural. It is not unwillingness. I have been asking.

What is actually in motion

  • A treating specialist at South West Healthcare, who has said plainly that this is beyond what she is equipped to manage alone.
  • An echocardiogram booked for 20 August 2026, which answers a separate cardiac question.
  • A name for a contact at the Warrnambool Adult Mental Health Team. Nothing has been actioned on it yet.
  • Public community mental health, which would not carry a gap fee, is the open question to chase.

The other two barriers

Transport. No licence, Koroit to Warrnambool for everything. It is part of why the earliest GP appointment I could take is 1 October 2026.

Housing. I have been without secure housing since early 2025, across multiple placements, and I am currently in a caravan. Every clinical recommendation I have been given assumes a stable base I do not have.

pages.title: Who to Call
pages.content:
Immediate danger. Chest pain, breathlessness, confusion, or a safety concern.

000

South West Healthcare, Mental Health Triage. 24 hours, Warrnambool and Glenelg region.

1800 808 284

This is the right first call for a mental health concern that is not an emergency. It is not a last resort. If you are holding my phone because I handed it to you, this is the number.

Nurse-on-Call. 24 hours, physical health and triage advice.

1300 60 60 24

Lifeline. 24 hours.

13 11 14

My treating specialist. Specialist Outpatient Clinic, South West Healthcare, Ryot Street Warrnambool.

(03) 5563 1256

If I am being assessed or admitted, say these two things

  • I have a documented troponin-antibody false positive on record. This must be stated at triage before any bloods are drawn, or a cardiac result will be misread.
  • Allergy: isosorbide mononitrate.

My full medical handover, including cardiac history and current medications, is at mahda.com.au/medical. It has a clinical view built for handing a phone to a stranger.

pages.title: Common Questions
pages.content:
He seems completely fine. Sharp, productive, on top of everything. Are you sure?

That is the pattern, not evidence against it. See The Pattern.

Should I call someone right now?

If there is a direct safety concern, yes, call 000. Otherwise the mental health triage line is the correct first call rather than something to hold off on. See Who to Call.

Why hasn't he just seen a psychologist?

Because of cost, availability and transport, not reluctance. What's Missing sets it out in full.

Is any of this actually diagnosed, or is it self-assessed?

Diagnosed. The formal picture, and who by, is on What's On Record.

Has anything ever worked?

Yes. A four week PARC admission in 2025. That is why getting back into structured support is the goal rather than an open question.

What do I actually say to him?

Plainly, and once. Saying it clearly the first time works. Repeating it four ways does not.

Why does this page exist instead of him just telling people?

Because writing it once, carefully, when thinking is easy works better than explaining it live, in the moment, when it usually is not.

Can I share this link?

Please don't. It is unlisted and I send it to people directly. If you think someone should see it, ask me first.
